items.title: Is Minimum Wage A Price Floor? Understanding Labor Economics
items.excerpt: Minimum wage laws are often cited as a classic example of a price floor, which is a government-imposed minimum price set above the equilibrium level in a market. In this context, the price refers to the wage rate, and the law establishes the lowest amount employers can legally pay their workers.
